claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children that you're looking to claim Child Benefit for?** If yes, how many children do you have, and what are their ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child - Alex, who is 18 years old and lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I can see you have one child, Alex, who is 18 years old and lives with you at home.

Since Alex is 18, I need to ask an important follow-up question:

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is Alex in sixth form, college, doing A-levels, or in an approved training program?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in any education or training at the moment. They finished school and haven't continued with any courses.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I need to ask one more question to complete my assessment:

**Is Alex currently working?** If yes, how many hours per week does Alex work?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't working at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me assess Alex's eligibility for Child Benefit based on what you've told me.

Based on the rules:
- You normally qualify for Child Benefit for a child under 16
- For children aged 16-19, you can still qualify if they stay in approved education or training
- Child Benefit stops if your child is 16 or over and starts paid work for 24 hours or more a week and is no longer in approved education or training

In Alex's situation:
- Alex is 18 years old
- Alex is not in approved education or training
- Alex is not working

Since Alex is over 16 and is **not** in approved education or training, you would not be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex, regardless of whether Alex is working or not. The key requirement for children aged 16-19 is that they must be in approved education or training.

I'm sorry, but based on your circumstances, **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

The reason is that while Child Benefit normally covers children under 16, for young people aged 16-19 (like Alex who is 18), they must be in approved education or training for you to continue receiving Child Benefit. Since Alex has finished school and is not continuing with any courses or training, you don't qualify for Child Benefit.

If Alex were to start approved education or training in the future (such as college, A-levels, or an approved training program), you could then apply for Child Benefit at that time.
